annotations.title: Find the source of a quotation (alpha)

description:
Check each result against the source text (link provided).
Finds where a quoted passage comes from: paste the quotation alone (a sentence or a paragraph, 3,000 characters at most), in its original language. Returns the statutory texts and decisions that contain it, with a match percentage (100 = word for word, once line breaks, punctuation, case and accents are removed) and the word-by-word differences (changed agreement, missing word…). Statuses: trouve (word for word); trouve_avec_differences (read differences); non_trouve (the database may be incomplete); trop_court (too short); trop_courant (passage too common to point to one source); indetermine (nothing found, but some sources did not answer in time: retry). Statutory texts containing the passage are in `textes_d_origine`, decisions that quote it in `repris_dans`; without a statutory text, `decisions` starts with the oldest one found. Sources: codes and statutes (`version_du` = date of the version used), Journal officiel, collective agreements (the article, its agreement and IDCC), administrative and ordinary case law (including Judilibre), Conseil constitutionnel, ECHR, CJEU, CNIL, doctrine (CADA, Défenseur des droits, conclusions, BOFiP), codes of ethics and professional rules (doctors, lawyers, notaries…, canon law). EU legislation (regulations, directives) is NOT in the database: `note_textes_europeens` says so.

Example: check_citations(text="Les obligations naissent d'actes juridiques, de faits juridiques ou de l'autorité seule de la loi.")
